top_3_arguments: Analyst consensus limits upside to ~8%: avg_price_target = $166.60 vs current $154.44, and the Street is 24 Hold vs 11 Buy vs 1 Sell — the majority sees the restructuring story as already reflected in price. A breakout through $156 watch level requires a move into territory where only the two most bullish houses (JP Morgan $185, Canaccord $175) provide cover; the consensus crowd is not chasing this. Poor asymmetry for a breakout trade: paying up through resistance with only 7.9% to consensus mean.

Spinoff execution risk is live and time-compressed: the Midera Food Processing spinoff (share distribution to existing stockholders) is targeted for early July 2026 — roughly 5 weeks away, pending regulatory approval. Spinoffs routinely create forced selling as index funds, income-oriented holders, and institutional mandates that cannot hold the new entity dump both parent and stub shares in the weeks before and around the distribution date. Management guided margin recovery to H2 2026 on the assumption 'tariff headwinds ease' — this is a conditional, not confirmed, and the spinoff adds operational distraction risk exactly when execution matters most.

Bearish RSI divergence on the daily timeframe (rsi_divergence.bearish = true) coincides with a vertical 5-day price spike (roc_5d = +9.13%) and an rsi_7 reading of 82.63 — extreme short-term overbought. The stock is now 8.7% above the 50-SMA and running into a volume-confirmed hourly pivot resistance at $154.71 (6 tests, volume confirmed) that sits just $0.27 above the current close of $154.44. Daily volume at the breakout attempt is exactly 1.0x the 20-day average (current 672,500 vs avg 673,545) — no institutional accumulation signal; hourly relative_volume is 0.10, meaning the late-day push that built this close is thin. Zero insider purchases in recent_insider_trades despite a headline restructuring catalyst that insiders would ordinarily buy into.
